findings.text: Young clearing with TLB maintenance over a run uses a scalar path for one entry lacking contiguity and a contiguous block path for larger or contiguous cases. The boolean outcome signals whether maintenance was performed.

Write protection over a run has a single entry fast path and a multi entry slow path. The fast path samples the entry once and expands a contiguous block when flagged, dropping the flag from the cached copy before applying protection to avoid rereading. Callers promise presence so only contiguity is tested.

Write protecting a whole contiguous block preserves contiguity and depends on a subsequent collective invalidation, with visibility beforehand unspecified and protection guaranteed afterwards. A partial block must first be expanded because keeping contiguity while protecting only members would leave later hardware behavior unpredictable.
Single entry write protect is an architecture override that forwards to the multi entry routine with a count of one.

Access flag updates first normalize the incoming entry to noncontiguous form. They then use a scalar path when the stored entry is not a valid contiguous entry and a contiguous path otherwise. Updates only widen permissions and track access and dirty state.

Contiguous access flag update follows three outcomes. When every member already carries the requested access and write state it reports no change. When write permission is unchanged it rewrites the whole aligned block without expansion and issues at most one range flush when dirty handling was requested. When write permission changes it expands around the target then performs one update. Return separates changed from unchanged.

Members of a contiguous block must share consistent attributes because hardware may cache any member as the representative mapping. Walkers that inspect entries one by one without coalesced hardware updates could otherwise keep faulting on a target whose sibling was updated, for reads missing accessed state and writes still marked read only. The check therefore scans the entire block from raw values rather than a gathered view.

Whole block access comparison starts from the aligned block base and tests only the controls consumed by access updates, namely read only versus writable, accessed and dirty indications. Address and unrelated control differences are ignored.
Young and dirty clearing over a run uses a scalar helper for one noncontiguous entry and a contiguous helper for other cases.

Contiguous young and dirty clearing widens any partially covered block to its full aligned extent before clearing. This is justified by folio granularity accounting and by forming contiguous blocks only within a single folio.

In the noncontiguous build every public page table helper aliases directly to its scalar double underscore counterpart, covering fetch, install, bulk install, clear, full clear, fetch and clear, young query and flush, write protect and access flag operations.
Protection keys support eight values selected by three mapping flag bits.

Keys are usable only when overlay permission hardware is present. Allocation state is a per context bitmask with one bit per key. Allocation fails when disabled or full, else returns the lowest free index and marks it used. Key zero is implicitly allocated at creation. Release rejects unknown or out of range values and otherwise clears the bit.

Protection override prefers an explicitly supplied key and otherwise keeps the mapping current key. Execute only queries always report absence because that mode is served by separate privilege hardware.
Authentication key material is two machine words. Per thread user state holds five such keys for instruction A and B, data A and B, and generic use. Kernel state holds one instruction A key.

Kernel initialization randomizes the kernel key only with address authentication available, and kernel switching installs that key followed by a barrier. User installation writes instruction B and data keys only with address authentication available and the generic key only with generic authentication available. User initialization randomizes the applicable keys then installs them.

Enabling turns on all four address authentication controls plus a barrier, doing nothing without that feature. User thread setup initializes keys and enables all address keys. Suspend, exit and task switch paths reinstall the relevant user keys. Kernel thread setup and switch delegate to kernel init and switch helpers.

Without authentication support, enable, suspend, thread setup and thread switch are no operations, while reset and key query or update helpers fail with invalid argument. Kernel thread setup and switch are likewise no operations.

User and kernel authentication code masks are ranges whose low bound tracks live virtual address width, with the user top near bit 54 and the kernel top at bit 63. The manageable key mask combines instruction and data A and B selectors.
Initial overlay permission value grants full access under key zero.
Reschedule request occupies bit 32 and the enabled count value equals that bit alone. Fresh tasks start from dedicated fork and idle initial counts.

Preemption state packs a low counter and a reschedule indication into one 64 bit word with inverted indication storage where zero means requested and one means clear. Count adjustments leave the indication untouched. Decrement and test touches only the low counter and reports true when the stored word becomes fully zero or a reread observes zero, tolerating a concurrent interrupt clearing the indication between separate read and write steps. A separate predicate tests whole word equality against a caller offset.
Preemption entry points alias either to dynamic patch variants or to direct scheduler calls according to build, separately for normal and no trace forms.

Probe handling uses a callback receiving operation code, address and register state. An architecture probe record holds that callback. Probe operation codes are little endian 32 bit values. Instruction state pairs the probe record with an out of line buffer pointer and a restore address used after stepping that buffer.

Network alignment is zero. Tagging control packs a 16 bit user exclusion field at the low end plus single bit selectors for sync, async and asymmetric fault modes and for store only checking. The 32 bit task size is four gibibytes in one build and one page less in another. The 32 bit vector base sits near the top of that range.

The 64 bit task size and default mapping window are powers of two derived from minimum and live address widths, with the maximum from the architectural width. Mixed mode builds choose task size, window and stack top by testing a per thread or per task compatibility flag, while pure 64 bit builds use 64 bit values unconditionally. Stack maximum follows task size or default window by build, unmapped base aligns one quarter of the applicable size, and mmap end and base helpers clamp requests crossing the default window.

Keeping contiguity while changing write permission over members, or leaving members with divergent access attributes, risks unpredictable translations and repeated faults on walkers without coalesced updates. Write protect visibility is unspecified until deferred invalidation completes. Young and dirty clearing deliberately affects whole blocks so per page precision is lost.

Count updates use separate read and write steps that can race with interrupts. Only the decrement and test path rereads to recover a concurrently cleared reschedule indication, so other adjustment paths need an environment where such races are excluded. Counter stores must never disturb the packed flag.
Headers use include guards to prevent multiple inclusion.
